wood.name: Wood
wood.description: Tamarack or hardwood, fire-cured and bound with rawhide. Any village can make one in a morning.
wood.whyHere: Hist-bark bows and fire-cured hardwood are the marsh's oldest working kit; any village makes them.

studded.name: Studded
studded.description: Crocodile hide riveted with bog iron. Light.
studded.whyHere: Crocodile and hackwing hide riveted with bog iron is what the marsh's hunters wear.

iron.name: Iron
iron.description: Bog iron, heavy and soft. What a levy or a work gang is handed.
iron.whyHere: Bog iron is the marsh's working metal, smelted in small works for levies and gangs.

bronze.name: Bronze
bronze.description: Copper alloy, hammered and edged by a village smith. It is made in the marsh.
bronze.whyHere: Saxhleel smiths worked bronze before the Duskfall and still edge their blades with copper alloy.
sources: King of the Murkmire.esp:COBJ TemperSaxhleelSword IngotCorundum

steel.name: Steel
steel.description: Trade steel with a copper-bright edge. It is imported.
steel.whyHere: Imperial, Dunmer and pirate traders bring in steel; local smiths give it a copper edge.

bone.name: Bone
bone.description: Beast-bone, ground to an edge and lashed with sinew. It holds that edge for one fight.
bone.whyHere: The Naga-Kur and Xit-Xaht make weapons and plate from bone. Grave-singers harvest it.

imperial.name: Imperial
imperial.description: Legion pattern, forged for a shield wall, now stacked in a levy store.
imperial.whyHere: The Legion garrisoned the marsh for millennia and its levies inherited the pattern.

silver.name: Silver
silver.description: Soft metal. It harms the undead.
silver.whyHere: Argonians work silver into frill clips and flutes. The Collections traded it.

dwarven.name: Dwarven
dwarven.description: Dwemer alloy, still bright after four thousand years.
dwarven.whyHere: Dwemer metal came south in Dunmer colonial trade and as spoil from the war of 4E 6.

elven.name: Elven
elven.whyHere: Aldmeri invaders and Maormer sea raiders left elven kit along the coast and rivers.

orcish.name: Orcish
orcish.description: Orichalcum, beaten thick. Built to break things.
orcish.whyHere: Orsimer mercenaries took Imperial pay in the province. Their arms remain.

falmer.name: Chitin
falmer.description: Chitin lashed to bone, sting-edged. It smells of the swamp.
falmer.whyHere: Chitin, horn and bone are working materials here; giant wasps and mudcrabs supply the shell.

forsworn.name: Hackwing
forsworn.description: Hackwing hide, feather and bone, bound with cord. Light enough for running.
forsworn.whyHere: Hackwing hide and plumage is what the marsh's hunters prize above any other.

akaviri.name: Akaviri
akaviri.description: Akaviri folded steel, left by the invaders of 2E 572. No smith in the marsh can make it.
akaviri.whyHere: The Akaviri invaders of 2E 572 were driven into the sea across Thorn and Stormhold. Their steel remains.

glass.name: Glass
glass.description: Malachite, ground to a hard, brittle edge.
glass.whyHere: Malachite plate is a Dunmer-war and Imperial luxury. Argonians work glass themselves.

obsidian.name: Volcanic Glass
obsidian.description: Volcanic glass knapped to a green-black edge, from the xanmeers. It cuts deeper than steel, but it chips.
obsidian.whyHere: Pre-Duskfall Argonians knapped volcanic glass for the weapons found in xanmeers.

ebony.name: Ebony
ebony.description: The blood of a god, cooled and hammered flat.
ebony.whyHere: Ebony came south as Dunmer trade and as spoil from the sack of Mournhold in 4E 6.

daedric.name: Daedric
daedric.description: Ebony quenched in a heart still beating. It does not rust.
daedric.whyHere: Dagon's war parties and the ruin of Ten-Maur-Wolk leave daedric arms in the marsh.
